_meta.notes: Comprehensive index for Mexico covering Olmec (mother culture), Teotihuacán, Maya (Palenque, Chichén Itzá), Zapotec/Mixtec (Monte Albán), Toltec, Aztec/Mexica (Tenochtitlán, largest city in Americas), Cortés conquest 1519-21, New Spain viceroyalty (300 years), Hidalgo Grito 1810, independence 1821, Mexican-American War (lost half territory), Juarez/Reform War, Maximilian/French intervention, Porfirio Díaz Porfiriato, Mexican Revolution 1910-20, PRI 71-year rule, NAFTA, drug war 2006-present, and AMLO/Sheinbaum.

official_languages: Spanish (de facto; no official at federal level)

religion.note: Most populous Spanish-speaking Catholic country; Virgen de Guadalupe (1531, central to national identity, patroness of Americas); syncretic folk Catholicism (Santa Muerte, curanderismo); evangelical growth in south/indigenous areas; Día de los Muertos (indigenous-Catholic fusion, UNESCO)

ethnic_groups.name: Mestizo
ethnic_groups.notes: Mixed Indigenous-European; national identity built on mestizaje ideology (post-Revolution); la raza cósmica (Vasconcelos); culturally dominant; encompasses wide range of phenotypes

ethnic_groups.name: Indigenous
ethnic_groups.notes: ~25.7M (self-identified/language); Náhuatl (Aztec descendants, ~2.5M speakers); Maya (~800,000 speakers); Zapotec; Mixtec; Purépecha; Tarahumara/Rarámuri; 68 recognized languages; EZLN Zapatista movement 1994 (Chiapas, Subcomandante Marcos); autonomy demands; poverty disproportionate

ethnic_groups.name: White (European descent)
ethnic_groups.notes: Spanish, also French, German, Italian, Lebanese; criollo elite historically; telenovela/media overrepresentation; concentrated in north/cities (Monterrey, Guadalajara)

ethnic_groups.name: Afro-Mexican
ethnic_groups.notes: ~2.6M (2020 census, first count); Costa Chica (Guerrero/Oaxaca); Veracruz; descendants of enslaved Africans (colonial era); historically invisible; recognized constitutionally 2019; Yanga (first free African town in Americas, 1609)

ethnic_groups.name: Other (Arab, Asian, etc.)
ethnic_groups.notes: Lebanese descent (~400,000+, Carlos Slim richest person in Americas); Chinese (Mexicali, historically persecuted); Japanese; Mennonites (Chihuahua); Jewish; Korean

country_profile.notes_unique: Largest Spanish-speaking country by population; 35 UNESCO World Heritage Sites (7th most in world); Aztec/Tenochtitlán built on lake (Mexico City sinking); Mexican-American War 1846-48 (lost Texas, California, New Mexico, Arizona, 55% of territory); Mexican Revolution 1910-20 (~2M dead, Zapata/Villa/Carranza); PRI one-party rule 71 years (1929-2000); NAFTA/USMCA; drug war 2006-present (~450,000+ dead, cartels: Sinaloa, CJNG); Carlos Slim (richest in Americas); muralism (Rivera, Orozco, Siqueiros); Día de los Muertos; Virgen de Guadalupe; tequila/tacos; Frida Kahlo; EZLN Zapatistas

current_leader.name: Claudia Sheinbaum
current_leader.title: President
current_leader.notes: First female president; MORENA; scientist (IPCC Nobel co-recipient); AMLO successor; former Mexico City mayor; Jewish-Bulgarian/Sephardic descent; landslide victory

former_leaders.name: Andrés Manuel López Obrador (AMLO)
former_leaders.notes: MORENA; left-populist; 'Fourth Transformation'; austerity for officials; social programs; morning press conferences; AMLO-ism; military expansion; judicial reform controversy; 65%+ approval; polarizing

former_leaders.name: Enrique Peña Nieto
former_leaders.notes: PRI return; Pact for Mexico reforms (energy, education); 43 Ayotzinapa students disappeared 2014 (Iguala); corruption scandals ('White House'); unpopular

former_leaders.name: Felipe Calderón
former_leaders.notes: PAN; launched drug war December 2006 (deployed military, ~120,000 killed during term); disputed election (0.58% margin vs AMLO); security crisis architect

former_leaders.name: Vicente Fox
former_leaders.notes: PAN; ended 71 years of PRI rule (first opposition president); Coca-Cola executive; democratic transition; migration reform attempted; disappointing reforms

former_leaders.name: Ernesto Zedillo
former_leaders.notes: PRI; peso crisis 1994-95 (tequila crisis); EZLN conflict; democratic opening (allowed PAN to win 2000); Yale professor after

former_leaders.name: Carlos Salinas de Gortari
former_leaders.notes: PRI; NAFTA architect; neoliberal modernization; 1988 stolen election ('se cayó el sistema'); brother arrested for murder; fled Mexico

former_leaders.name: Porfirio Díaz
former_leaders.notes: Porfiriato; 35-year dictatorship; 'Order and Progress'; railroad/modernization; extreme inequality; French culture imitation; overthrown by Revolution 1910; died in Paris exile

former_leaders.name: Benito Juárez
former_leaders.notes: Zapotec indigenous lawyer; greatest Mexican president; Reform Laws (seized Church property); defeated French intervention; executed Maximilian; 'Among individuals as among nations, respect for the rights of others is peace'; 5 terms; died in office

910.name: Olmec Civilization (Mother Culture)
910.description: First major Mesoamerican civilization: colossal heads, ceremonial centres at San Lorenzo and La Venta, ballgame, calendar systems.

sub_clusters.name: San Lorenzo Phase
sub_clusters.description: Earliest Olmec centre, colossal basalt heads, monumental earthworks, hierarchical society.

sub_clusters.name: La Venta Phase
sub_clusters.description: Great Pyramid, jade offerings, Olmec artistic and religious influence spreads across Mesoamerica.

sub_clusters.name: Olmec Cultural Diffusion
sub_clusters.description: Spread of Olmec iconography, writing, ballgame, Long Count calendar origins to successor cultures.

910.name: Preclassic Maya in Mexico
910.description: Early Maya development in Chiapas, Tabasco, and the Yucatán Peninsula before the Classic period.

sub_clusters.name: Early Maya Settlements
sub_clusters.description: Village agriculture, early pottery, emergence of social complexity at sites like Cuello and Lamanai.

sub_clusters.name: Late Preclassic Maya
sub_clusters.description: Monumental architecture, E-Group complexes, early writing, Kaminaljuyú and Calakmul precursors.

910.name: Zapotec Civilization and Monte Albán
910.description: Oaxacan highland civilization: Monte Albán, earliest Mesoamerican writing, Danzantes reliefs.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of Monte Albán
sub_clusters.description: Hilltop capital construction, conquest slabs, astronomical observatory.

sub_clusters.name: Classic Monte Albán
sub_clusters.description: Peak population, Teotihuacan contacts, elaborate tombs, Zapotec script.

sub_clusters.name: Mixtec Successor States
sub_clusters.description: Mixtec takeover of Oaxacan sites, codices, goldworking, political fragmentation.

920.name: Teotihuacan — City of the Gods
920.description: One of the largest cities in the ancient world: Pyramids of the Sun and Moon, Avenue of the Dead, pan-Mesoamerican influence.

sub_clusters.name: Rise of Teotihuacan
sub_clusters.description: Monumental construction, Pyramid of the Sun, planned grid city, population over 100,000.

sub_clusters.name: Teotihuacan at Apex
sub_clusters.description: Talud-tablero architecture, murals, long-distance trade, diplomatic influence on Maya cities.

sub_clusters.name: Collapse of Teotihuacan
sub_clusters.description: Ritual burning of ceremonial centre, population decline, political fragmentation.

920.name: Classic Maya in Mexican Territory
920.description: Flourishing Maya city-states in Chiapas, Campeche, and Yucatán: Palenque, Calakmul, Uxmal.

sub_clusters.name: Palenque and the Dynasty of Pakal
sub_clusters.description: K'inich Janaab Pakal's reign, Temple of the Inscriptions, exquisite stucco art.

sub_clusters.name: Calakmul — Snake Dynasty Superpower
sub_clusters.description: Rival to Tikal, Kaan dynasty, vast political network across the Petén and beyond.

sub_clusters.name: Terminal Classic and Puuc Style
sub_clusters.description: Uxmal, Kabah, Sayil; elaborately decorated façades, Maya collapse dynamics in the lowlands.

920.name: Toltec Empire
920.description: Post-Classic warrior state at Tula (Tollan), Quetzalcoatl legend, Mesoamerican militarism.

sub_clusters.name: Founding of Tula
sub_clusters.description: Toltec capital establishment, Atlantean warrior columns, Quetzalcoatl–Tezcatlipoca mythology.

sub_clusters.name: Toltec Influence and Chichén Itzá
sub_clusters.description: Toltec stylistic impact on Chichén Itzá, feathered serpent imagery, Tula's eventual destruction.

930.name: Aztec Empire (Mexica Triple Alliance)
930.description: Rise of Tenochtitlan, Mexica dominance over central Mexico, tribute empire, Aztec cosmology and sacrifice.

sub_clusters.name: Foundation of Tenochtitlan
sub_clusters.description: Founding on Lake Texcoco island, eagle-on-cactus legend, Mexica rise from tributary status.

sub_clusters.name: Triple Alliance and Imperial Expansion
sub_clusters.description: Itzcoatl and Montezuma I forge the Triple Alliance with Texcoco and Tlacopan; rapid conquest, flower wars.

sub_clusters.name: Montezuma II and Aztec Apex
sub_clusters.description: Empire at maximum extent, tribute economy, Templo Mayor, population of 5-6 million subjects.

930.name: Spanish Conquest of Mexico
930.description: Hernán Cortés's expedition, Tlaxcalan alliance, fall of Tenochtitlan, and the end of the Aztec world.

sub_clusters.name: Cortés Expedition and March Inland
sub_clusters.description: Landing at Veracruz, Tlaxcalan alliance, Cholula massacre, Montezuma's capture, Noche Triste.

sub_clusters.name: Siege and Fall of Tenochtitlan
sub_clusters.description: 80-day siege, smallpox devastation, Cuauhtémoc's surrender, destruction of the city.

930.name: Viceroyalty of New Spain
930.description: Three centuries of Spanish colonial rule: encomienda, casta system, silver mining, Baroque culture, Bourbon reforms.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Foundations and Encomienda
sub_clusters.description: Mexico City built on Tenochtitlan ruins, encomienda system, mass conversion, demographic collapse.

sub_clusters.name: Silver Mining Economy
sub_clusters.description: Zacatecas, Guanajuato, Potosí supply chain; silver peso as global currency, mita/repartimiento labour.

sub_clusters.name: Colonial Baroque Culture
sub_clusters.description: Sor Juana Inés de la Cruz, cathedral construction, syncretic religiosity, Churrigueresque architecture.

sub_clusters.name: Bourbon Reforms
sub_clusters.description: Administrative centralisation, economic liberalisation, Creole resentment, Enlightenment ideas.

940.name: Mexican Independence
940.description: Independence struggle from Hidalgo's Grito de Dolores to Iturbide's Plan de Iguala.

sub_clusters.name: Hidalgo's Revolt
sub_clusters.description: Grito de Dolores (16 Sep 1810), peasant army, Virgin of Guadalupe banner, Hidalgo's capture and execution.

sub_clusters.name: Morelos and the Insurgent State
sub_clusters.description: José María Morelos continues the fight, Congress of Chilpancingo, Sentimientos de la Nación, royalist victory.

sub_clusters.name: Iturbide and Final Independence
sub_clusters.description: Plan de Iguala, Three Guarantees, Iturbide's short-lived empire, independence declared 1821.

940.name: Early Republic and Instability
940.description: First Empire, Republic, caudillo politics, Texas secession, and the catastrophic Mexican-American War.

sub_clusters.name: First Empire and Federal Republic
sub_clusters.description: Iturbide's empire collapses, 1824 Constitution, federalist vs. centralist struggles.

sub_clusters.name: Texas Secession
sub_clusters.description: Texan revolt, Santa Anna at the Alamo and San Jacinto, loss of Texas.

sub_clusters.name: Mexican-American War
sub_clusters.description: US invasion, fall of Mexico City, Treaty of Guadalupe Hidalgo — Mexico loses half its territory.

940.name: La Reforma and French Intervention
940.description: Juárez's liberal reforms, War of the Reform, French occupation, Emperor Maximilian, and the restored Republic.

sub_clusters.name: Juárez and the Reform Laws
sub_clusters.description: Ley Juárez, Ley Lerdo, separation of church and state, War of the Reform (1858-61).

sub_clusters.name: French Intervention and Emperor Maximilian
sub_clusters.description: Napoleon III's intervention, Battle of Puebla (5 May 1862), Maximilian's Habsburg empire, Juárez's resistance, Maximilian's execution.

940.name: The Porfiriato
940.description: Porfirio Díaz's long dictatorship: modernisation, railroads, foreign investment, inequality, and repression.

sub_clusters.name: Porfirian Modernization
sub_clusters.description: Railway expansion, mining concessions, científicos, order and progress at the cost of land dispossession.

sub_clusters.name: Crisis of the Porfiriato
sub_clusters.description: Cananea and Río Blanco strikes, Madero's challenge, Plan de San Luis Potosí, Díaz's exile.

950.name: Mexican Revolution
950.description: Decade of armed upheaval: Madero, Zapata, Villa, Carranza, Constitution of 1917.

sub_clusters.name: Madero Uprising and Decena Trágica
sub_clusters.description: Madero's revolution, presidency, Huerta coup and assassination.

sub_clusters.name: Zapatismo and Villismo
sub_clusters.description: Plan de Ayala, Zapata's agrarian revolution, Villa's División del Norte, Columbus raid.

sub_clusters.name: Constitution of 1917
sub_clusters.description: Revolutionary charter: Article 27 (land reform), Article 123 (labour rights), Article 3 (secular education).

sub_clusters.name: Revolutionary Aftermath
sub_clusters.description: Carranza's presidency, Zapata's assassination (1919), Obregón's coup, revolution's consolidation.

950.name: Post-Revolutionary Mexico and PRI Era
950.description: Institutional revolution: PNR/PRM/PRI, Cárdenas oil nationalisation, Mexican Miracle, cultural renaissance.

sub_clusters.name: Institutional Revolution (Calles to Cárdenas)
sub_clusters.description: Maximato, Cristero War, PNR creation (1929), Cárdenas land reform, PEMEX oil expropriation (1938).

sub_clusters.name: Mexican Miracle (Import Substitution)
sub_clusters.description: Rapid industrialization, GDP growth, urbanization, 1968 Olympics, Tlatelolco massacre.

sub_clusters.name: Muralism and Cultural Renaissance
sub_clusters.description: Rivera, Orozco, Siqueiros murals; Frida Kahlo, Octavio Paz, national cultural identity.

950.name: Late PRI Era and Crises
950.description: Dirty War, 1982 debt crisis, 1985 earthquake, NAFTA, Zapatista uprising, democratic transition.

sub_clusters.name: Dirty War and Political Repression
sub_clusters.description: State repression of dissent, Halconazo (1971), guerrilla movements, disappearances.

sub_clusters.name: Debt Crisis and Neoliberal Turn
sub_clusters.description: 1982 default, structural adjustment, privatisation, Salinas reforms, NAFTA (1994).

sub_clusters.name: Zapatista Uprising (EZLN)
sub_clusters.description: Indigenous revolt in Chiapas on NAFTA launch day, Subcomandante Marcos, San Andrés Accords.

960.name: Democratic Transition
960.description: End of 71-year PRI rule, Fox and Calderón presidencies, electoral democracy, drug war escalation.

sub_clusters.name: Fox's Victory and End of PRI Hegemony
sub_clusters.description: Vicente Fox (PAN) wins 2000 election, democratic alternation, limited reform.

sub_clusters.name: Calderón and the War on Drugs
sub_clusters.description: Military offensive against cartels, 60,000+ killed, Sinaloa-Zetas rivalry, human rights crisis.

960.name: Drug Trafficking and Organised Violence
960.description: Rise of cartels, narco-violence, Ayotzinapa disappearances, militarised security, migration consequences.

sub_clusters.name: Cartel Wars and Fragmentation
sub_clusters.description: Sinaloa, CJNG, Zetas; territorial control, mass graves, journalists targeted.

sub_clusters.name: Ayotzinapa Disappearances
sub_clusters.description: 43 Normalista students disappeared in Iguala, state complicity, ongoing investigation.

960.name: AMLO and the Fourth Transformation (4T)
960.description: López Obrador's MORENA presidency, social programmes, austerity, judicial reform, Sheinbaum succession.

sub_clusters.name: AMLO Presidency
sub_clusters.description: Landslide victory, austerity, Tren Maya, National Guard, 'abrazos no balazos' security policy.

sub_clusters.name: USMCA/T-MEC and Trade Relations
sub_clusters.description: NAFTA renegotiation, nearshoring boom, Tesla Gigafactory, US-Mexico migration diplomacy.

sub_clusters.name: Sheinbaum and Post-AMLO Era
sub_clusters.description: First woman president, judicial reform controversy, 4T continuity, climate and energy debates.

unassigned_events.note: Events not yet assigned to a thematic cluster
